summary: Dock topology changes can expose a stale BlurImageControl completion callback.

judgment.rationale: Dock topology changes can expose a stale BlurImageControl completion callback. Hypothesis: an obsolete image completion survives image replacement/control teardown and touches disposed composition state. This is an initial investigation direction, not a runtime-confirmed diagnosis.
evidence: Two-monitor dock report supplies a ZIP and describes toggles/icons becoming incorrect before a crash.
Read the supplied CmdPal error reports: ObjectDisposedException reaches BlurImageControl.SetLoadedSurfaceToBrush from the LoadedImageSurface completion callback.

proposed_fixes.title: Dock topology changes can expose a stale BlurImageControl completion callback
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: an obsolete image completion survives image replacement/control teardown and touches disposed composition state.
plan: Trace surface generation and control unload/disposal during topology-driven dock reconstruction.
Unsubscribe obsolete callbacks and reject completions that no longer belong to the active surface/control before brush assignment.
Preserve real load-error reporting and test replacement/unload callbacks; do not merely swallow ObjectDisposedException.
verification: Repeated monitor connect/disconnect and image replacement do not crash or display stale imagery.
Current images still load and genuine image failures remain observable.
